**The YW line — the most contested philological data-point in the chapter, handled with exemplary lens-discipline.** Bare *YW* preserved in surface English (no vocalization commitment, no Hebrew-cognation pre-resolution); claim_type correctly `inferred` (not `direct`); all three named-scholarship readings (de Moor 1971, Cross 1973, Smith 1994 vol 1) documented; verbatim disavowal of the YHWH-originated-as-Canaanite-deity claim present in the central-entry rationale ('This entry does NOT claim that Ugaritic proves Yahweh originated as a Canaanite deity. The philological evidence is genuinely contested.'). Sitchin-engineered-ET-deity and Christian-Trinitarian/Yahweh-Christology pre-resolutions explicitly disavowed. This is the single most-important lens-discipline site in the chapter and the Editor's handling is fully defensible by Smith / Cross / Day scholarship standards.

Possible Hebrew Bible echo in the Isa 2:4 / Mic 4:3 swords-into-plowshares peace-oracle, though the parallels are typological rather than philologically cognate.

[tranquility into the midst of the field]s. Hasten —
[urge, speed; to me your fe]et — let them race;
[to me let your leg]s hasten — to the midst of the mountain.
[…] in your hand the message-tablet,

[KTU 1.1 col iii: top of column lost. Preserved text addresses Kothar-wa-Khasis (the divine craftsman), summoning him from his Egyptian/Mediterranean abode at Kaphtor (= Crete) and Memphis. This is the cycle's introduction of the artisan-deity who will later forge Baʿlu's weapons in KTU 1.2 IV.]
[Kapht]or is the throne [of his seat; Memphis is the land of his inheritance];

notes.official: Kothar-wa-Khasis's Mediterranean-Egyptian abode: Kaphtor (= Crete; Ugaritic *kptr*) for his throne, Memphis (Ugaritic *ḥkpt*, from Egyptian *Hwt-kꜢ-Ptḥ* 'House of the soul of Ptah') for his land of inheritance. The geography situates the divine craftsman in the Late Bronze Age metal-and-glass-working centers; see central entry `kothar-wa-khasis-divine-craftsman-cross-corpus-speech-act-weapon-naming`.

notes.official: Kothar-wa-Khasis is introduced with his alternate name Hayin (Ugaritic *hyn*) — possibly etymologically 'craftsman' or possibly a separate divine figure conflated with Kothar. Smith 1994 vol 1 treats the two as equivalent. The binomial *kṯr w ḫss* 'Skillful-and-Clever' is the full standing form.

notes.official: The famous mystery-revelation formula *rgm ʿṣ w lḫšt ʾabn* — a fixed Ugaritic liturgical-formula for esoteric cosmic-communication. Smith 1994 vol 1 reads as fixed formula; Ginsberg 1955 reads more concretely as 'message of timber and stone'. Cross-corpus echo at Hab 2:11 (stone-and-timber crying out) and Ps 19:1-4 (heavens' speech). Central entry `word-of-tree-whisper-of-stone-mystery-revelation-formula-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible` covers (promoted from overlay at ch 2 Editor pass when formula recurred at KTU 1.3-iii).

i18n.en: the converse of heaven with [earth, of the deeps with the stars],

notes.official: Ugaritic *thmt* 'deeps' is the direct cognate of Hebrew *t'hôm* (Gen 1:2). Cross-corpus parallel with Ps 19:1-4 (heavens declare the glory of God) is widely discussed in Smith 1994 vol 1; the converse-between-cosmic-elements is the formula's cosmographic-scope marker.

notes.official: *ʿnn ʾilm* literally 'cloud-attendants of the gods' — divine messenger-class with cloud-traveling associations (*ʿnn* 'cloud'). Surface translation generalizes to 'attendants of the gods' to avoid pre-resolving the cloud-attendant register onto the later *rkb ʿrpt* 'Rider of the Clouds' epithet of Baʿlu (KTU 1.2-iv:6) or onto NT 'coming on clouds' Christology. The *bn ʾilm* / divine-assembly context governs the line (central entry `bn-ilm-sons-of-god-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bnei-elohim`).

notes.official: ʾIlu's epithet *ʾab šnm* 'Father of Years' — a major cross-corpus candidate with Dan 7:9 *ʿattîq yômîn* 'Ancient of Days', both paternal-eternity epithets of the head-of-pantheon. The surface English preserves 'Father of Years' literal form rather than substituting the Bible-resonant 'Ancient of Days', which would over-commit to a Daniel-typology pre-resolution.

Bull ʾIlu his fa[ther …]

in the midst of [...]

[KTU 1.1 col iv: top of column lost. The preserved text is the most substantive section of KTU 1.1 — the divine banquet at which ʾIlu proclaims Yammu's elevation, gives him the new name 'Yaw' (a striking parallel to Yahweh in the Hebrew Bible — Smith 1994 vol 1, pp. 151-160), and orders Baʿlu's expulsion from kingship. This is the political setup for the duel in KTU 1.2.]
[…] (signs uncertain) […]
Aloud he cried to Q[...]
to the distant ones, to P[...]
ʾIlu cried out; he sits at the m[arzeaḥ-feast …]

notes.official: *mrzḥ* — the formal ritual-banquet, with cross-corpus reach to Hebrew *marzēaḥ* (Amos 6:7 *bêt marzēaḥ*; Jer 16:5). Overlay entry `marzeah-ritual-banquet-baal-cycle-cross-reference-hebrew-bible` documents the institution (Pardee 2002; McLaughlin 2001).

a krpn-vessel in both hands [...]

ʾIlu guards his sons; the Bull [...]

lines.translit: w yʿn . lṭpn . ʾil . d p[ʾid ...]

i18n.en: And the Benevolent One, ʾIlu the kind-hearted, answered:
The name of my son is YW, O goddess [ʾIlatu …]

notes.official: **The YW line — the single most-contested Ugaritic-Hebrew comparative-philology data-point.** ʾIlu names a son YW (Ugaritic *yw*) at the divine banquet preceding Yammu's exaltation. Three named-scholarship readings on the YHWH-connection question: (a) de Moor 1971 reads YW as a real divine name, likely YHWH-related; (b) Cross 1973 is cautiously open; (c) Smith 1994 vol 1, pp. 152-160, is the most cautious — reads YW as one of ʾIlu's seventy sons being named, with the YHWH connection 'possible but not proven'. The Editor preserves bare transliteration YW with no vocalization-commitment. **This line does NOT prove that Yahweh originated as a Canaanite deity; the philological evidence is genuinely contested.** Central entry `yw-line-ktu-1-1-iv-14-proto-yahweh-candidate-cross-corpus-ugaritic` documents all three readings.

i18n.en: and he proclaimed the name of Yammu [...]

notes.official: ʾIlu proclaims (*pʿr*) Yammu's name. The verb *pʿr* 'to proclaim, declare' is the same speech-act-naming verb that Kothar uses for the weapon-naming at 1.2-iv:11 and 27 (central entry `yagrush-ayamur-speech-act-named-divine-weapons-cross-corpus`). Yammu's elevation is performatively-enacted by ʾIlu's speech-act-naming.

i18n.en: They answered him: We have not nourished(?) [...]
You are the lord — you shall proclaim [...]
I (am) the Benevolent One, ʾIlu [the kind-hearted …]
with raised hands I have proclaimed [...]
Your name is Beloved of ʾI[lu …]

notes.official: *mdd ʾil* 'Beloved of ʾIlu' — Yammu's standing epithet at his banquet-elevation. Compare Hebrew *yĕdîd* 'beloved' applied to Israel/Benjamin (Deut 33:12) and to Solomon (*Yedidyah*, 2 Sam 12:25), though the lexemes are not strictly cognate (*mdd* vs *ydd*; both proto-Semitic 'beloved' roots).

i18n.en: house of my silver, which [...]
from the hand of Mighty Baʿ[lu …]

notes.official: First occurrence of Baʿlu's standing epithet *ʾaliyn bʿl* 'Mighty Baʿlu' in the preserved text. The epithet is the most-frequent Baʿlu-designation across the Cycle. Central entry `baal-ugaritic-baalu-storm-god-cross-corpus-hebrew-bible-polemic` covers the storm-god's cross-corpus picture and the Hebrew polemic against Baʿal.

i18n.en: when he reviles me [...]

lines.translit: gršnn . l k[sʾi . mlkh . l nḫt . l kḥṯ]

i18n.en: drive him out from [the throne of his kingship, from the seat, from the dais]

notes.official: ʾIlu's kingship-deposition decree against Baʿlu. The throne-deposition formula *grš … l ksʾi mlkh* shares vocabulary with Isa 14:13 (Helal ben Shahar's deposition); Ezek 28 (Tyre); Ps 89:5. The verb *grš* 'drive out' is the same root as Yagrush ('Let-him-drive-out'), the weapon Kothar will later forge at 1.2-iv:12; it is also the verb of the Eden expulsion (Gen 3:24 *va-y'garesh et ha-adam*), but the Editor preserves 'drive him out' as the literal default rather than the Eden-resonant 'cast him out' to avoid pre-resolving the Gen 3 typology.

i18n.en: of his dominion [...]
and if also [...]
he will strike you like [...]
ʾIlu (held) a sacrifice [...]
he proclaimed at the house of [...]
He slaughtered ox[en; also sheep he laid low,]

i18n.en: bulls and [fatlings, rams, year-old calves],
lambs, [an abundance of kids …]

[KTU 1.1 col v: top destroyed. Preserved text contains fragmentary day-counting formulae and references to Mount Ṣapunu (Baʿlu's mountain), suggesting a transitional or travel scene. Smith 1994 vol 1 pp. 169-170 reads this as part of Baʿlu's escape or relocation following ʾIlu's deposition-decree.]
[… and a day, two day]s,
[they pass on; he arrives at] the throat (= appetite).
[… Had]du(?) — she meets him.

notes.official: *hd* = Haddu, the personal name of the storm-deity whose cult-title is Baʿlu. Cognate to Akkadian Adad and to Hebrew Bible Hadad (1 Kgs 11:14). Overlay entry `haddu-personal-name-of-the-storm-god-baal-cycle-1-1-v-overlay`.

i18n.en: […] in Ṣapunu.

notes.official: Mount Ṣapunu — Baʿlu's holy mountain, identified geographically with Jebel al-Aqra in modern Syria (1717m, called Mount Ḫazi in Akkadian, Kasion in Greek). Major cross-corpus to Hebrew *ṣāpôn* 'north' in fossilized cosmic-mountain attestations: Ps 48:3 *yarkĕtê ṣāpôn* applied to Mount Zion; Isa 14:13. Central entry `mount-sapunu-tsafon-cosmic-mountain-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible` (Clifford 1972; Cross 1973; Day 2000).

[…] then he answered:
[… I know that I have] not known.
[…] they bind.
[Bull ʾIlu …] he binds.
[…] stones, they were polished(?).
[…] and (with) the mountain of my loins,
[you who act presumptuously(?) …] the thinness of (his) back,
[…] all — she(?) opens(?) his loin.
[…] b — and a day, two days,
[they pass on …] he arrives at the throat.
[…] t — Haddu, she meets him.
[…] your wrath(?) in Ṣapunu.
[…] I will make a hind lie down.
[…] from the springs (of the deep) he answers.

notes.official: *mbkm* 'springs (of the deep)' — cross-corpus with Hebrew *nibkê tĕhôm* 'the springs of the deep' (Job 38:16), reflecting shared NW-Semitic cosmography of abyssal water-sources at the base of the cosmos. Day 1985 discusses; the parallel is widely cited.

i18n.en: […] I know; I have not known.
[…] they bind — Bull ʾIlu.
[…] he binds among the stones.
[…] they were polished(?); evening(?).
[… and] the mountain of my loins — you (act presumptuously?)
[…] she enters at the lifting(?).
[…] you shall not act presumptuously; you shall not tear apart(?).
[…] g[…] to the earth.
[KTU 1.1 col vi: destroyed — no preserved text. The end of tablet 1.1; transition to KTU 1.2 follows.]

[KTU 1.2 col i: opening lines fragmentary. The scene that unfolds: Yammu (the Sea-god) dispatches his two messengers (mlʾakm) to the divine assembly (pḫr mʿd) at Mount Lel, demanding the surrender of Baʿlu. ʾIlu and the gods abjectly submit; Baʿlu rages and must be restrained by ʿAnatu and ʿAṯtartu.]
[…] messenger of Yammu […]

notes.official: First clear occurrence of Yammu in the surviving text. The lemma *mlʾak* 'messenger' is the etymological source of Hebrew *malʾāk* (also 'angel') and ultimately Greek *angelos*. Surface renders as 'messenger' (neutral); the 'angel' gloss would risk anachronism in this Bronze Age divine-political context.

i18n.en: […] embassy of Judge Naharu (= River) […]

notes.official: *ṯpṭ nhr* 'Judge Naharu (= River)' — Yammu's binomial partner-name in standing parallelism Yammu // Naharu. The Yam/Nahar (Sea/River) doublet is itself a major comparative-mythology marker: cf. Hab 3:8 *ha-b-naharim charah YHWH … ʿal ha-yam ʿevratekha* matching exactly the Ugaritic yam//naharim doubling. The *ṯpṭ* 'Judge' title (cognate to Hebrew *šōpēṭ*) marks the judicial-royal authority claim Yammu makes against Baʿlu.

i18n.en: [They went a thousand-fold, going on, and ten thousand-fold like rain.]

i18n.en: [Naharu: Give up, O gods, the one whom you fear, whom the multitudes revere —]

i18n.en: [give up Baʿlu and his attendants — the Son of Daganu — that I may take his gold!]

notes.official: *bn dgn* 'Son of Daganu' — Baʿlu's standing paternity-epithet. Daganu is the Northwest-Semitic grain-deity, cross-corpus to Hebrew Bible Philistine Dagon (Judg 16:23; 1 Sam 5:2-7). The pḏ 'gold' (the booty Yammu demands) is contested: 'gold' (Gibson 1978, default) vs 'ransom' (Pardee 2003 cautious). Surface renders 'gold' for the literal default.

i18n.en: [The lads set out; they did not turn back. Then (their) face]

lines.translit: [l ytn . tk . ġr . ll . ʿm . pḫr . mʿd]

i18n.en: [was set toward Mount Lel, toward the gathered assembly.]

notes.official: *pḫr mʿd* 'gathered assembly' — the formal designation for the divine council at Mount Lel. Cross-corpus to Akkadian *puḫru ša ilāni* (Adapa, Enuma Elish) and to Hebrew *sod YHWH* / *ʿădat ʾēl* / *ʿădat qĕdōshîm* (Ps 89:8; Ps 82:1; Ps 89:6). The cluster is among the most-foundational cross-corpus divine-assembly attestations. Central entry `divine-council-phr-mad-cross-corpus-ugaritic-akkadian-hebrew-bible` (Mullen 1980; Heiser 2015; Cross 1973).

lines.translit: [ʾap . ʾilm . l lḥm . yṯb . bn . qdš]

i18n.en: [Indeed the gods had sat down to eat; the holy sons]

notes.official: *bn qdš* 'holy sons' — variant of *bn ʾilm* 'sons of god' designating the divine-council membership. **MAJOR cross-corpus** to Hebrew *bĕnê (hā)ʾĕlōhîm* (Gen 6:2, 4; Job 1:6, 2:1, 38:7; Ps 29:1, 89:7; Deut 32:8 LXX/4QDeut^j) and to *qĕdōshîm* 'holy ones' in divine-council contexts (Ps 89:6-8; Job 5:1; 15:15; Zech 14:5). Central entry `bn-ilm-sons-of-god-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bnei-elohim`. The entry's rationale documents the explicit disavowal of the WoH-Watchers-engineering reading of the Gen 6:2 / 1 Enoch material.

[saw them: they saw the messengers of Yammu, the embassy of Judge]

i18n.en: [Naharu. The gods lowered their heads onto the tops of their knees,]

notes.official: The gods' fearful posture before Yammu's envoys. Cross-corpus parallel sometimes drawn with Elijah's posture at Carmel (1 Kgs 18:42, head between knees), though the lamentation-posture inventory is broader and the parallel is typological rather than philological.

i18n.en: [and onto the daises of their princely-seats. Against them Baʿlu] rebukes:

notes.official: *ygʿr* 'rebukes' — major cross-corpus vocabulary: the *gāʿar* pattern of YHWH's rebuke of the sea / chaos-waters (Ps 18:15-16; Ps 104:7; Isa 17:13; Nah 1:4). This verb is one of the central Chaoskampf-rebuke lexemes shared across NW-Semitic; ʿAṯtartu reprises it at 1.2-iv:40 to seal Baʿlu's victory.

notes.official: The fire-and-sword-tongue topos of hostile messenger-speech. Cross-corpus with Hebrew Bible tongue-as-sword imagery: Ps 57:5 'their tongues are sharp swords'; Ps 64:4; Prov 12:18; cf. i18n.en: the Son of Daganu, that I may take his gold. And Bull, his father, ʾIlu answered:

lines.translit: ʿbdk . bʿl . y ymm . ʿbdk . bʿl

i18n.en: Your servant is Baʿlu, O Yammu! Your servant is Baʿlu,

notes.official: THE CONCESSION. ʾIlu submissively concedes Baʿlu to Yammu. The political crisis of the chapter. The literal 'your servant' is preserved over the stronger 'your slave' to preserve the deferential-vassal register that the Ugaritic *ʿbd* carries.

i18n.en: [O] Rivers! The Son of Daganu — your prisoner is he; he will bring (tribute),
your tribute, just as the gods [pay it…]
like the holy sons — gifts(?) for you [...]
But Prince Baʿlu was furious [...]

notes.official: *zbl bʿl* 'Prince Baʿlu' — standing epithet recurring through the Cycle. *zbl* is cognate to Hebrew *zĕbûl* 'lofty habitation' (1 Kgs 8:13; Hab 3:11; Ps 49:14) and to the personal/tribal name Zebulun.

i18n.en: [He took in his hand] a striking-(weapon); in (his) right hand a smiting-(weapon).

notes.official: Two obscure weapon-words. Smith 1994 vol 1 reads 'striking-weapon' and 'smiting-weapon' tentatively; Pardee 2003 leaves the line largely untranslated. These are **distinct** from the later named weapons Yagrush and Ayamur that Kothar will forge at 1.2-iv:10-31. Overlay entry `ast-mssst-obscure-weapon-words-baal-cycle-1-2-i-44` documents the editorial uncertainty.

lines.translit: ymnh . ʿnt . tʾuḫd . ymnh . ʿṯtrt . tʾuḫd [šmʾalh]

i18n.en: His right hand ʿAnatu seized; his right hand ʿAṯtartu seized [his left].

notes.official: One of the few preserved instances of ʿAnatu-ʿAṯtartu paired action (Walls 1992). The double-goddess restraint scene prevents Baʿlu from striking the messengers diplomatically immune by their status. ʿAṯtartu = Ugaritic ʿṯtrt; direct cognate of Hebrew Bible Ashtoreth (1 Kgs 11:5) and Greek Astarte.

lines.translit: ʾik . mġnt . [mlʾak] ym . tʿdt . ṯpṭ . nhr

i18n.en: How (can) you strike(?) the [messengers] of Yammu, the embassy of Judge Naharu?

[KTU 1.2 col ii: broken away entirely. The lost text is reconstructed from context (Smith 1994 vol 1 pp. 290-294): the central scene likely contained (i) Baʿlu's complaint or vow following the messengers' departure; (ii) the conference with Kothar-wa-Khasis (the divine craftsman); (iii) possibly the initial forging-instruction for the magical weapons Yagrush and Ayamur that will appear in column iv.]

[KTU 1.2 col iii: top of column lost. Preserved text contains a dialogue scene — possibly Kothar-wa-Khasis blessing Baʿlu's enterprise and predicting the defeat of his enemies; possibly also ʾAṯtart/ʿAnat petitioning ʾIlu on Baʿlu's behalf. Lineation per Smith 1994 vol 1.]
[And] Kothar-wa-Khasis [answered] […]
[to declare] to Mighty Baʿlu [...]
O ʾIwrkl(?), live(?) [...]

notes.official: Obscure form *ʾiwrkl* with no fixed reading; Smith 1994 vol 1 leaves untranslated. Overlay entry `iwrkl-obscure-name-or-epithet-baal-cycle-1-2-iii-6` documents the editorial uncertainty.

i18n.en: May Ḥôrânu(?) burn your he[ad …]

notes.official: Ḥôrânu is a minor underworld-or-curse-related Ugaritic deity (Smith 1994 vol 1). The parenthetical-query preserves the lexical uncertainty (Gibson 1978 reads as 'scorching curse' rather than as a deity). Cross-corpus to the Hebrew place-name Beth-Ḥôrôn is weak; overlay entry `horanu-minor-curse-deity-baal-cycle-1-2-iii-7`.

i18n.en: ʿAṯtartu — name of Baʿlu — (smash) your crown [...]

notes.official: *qdqd* 'crown of the head' — MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew *qodqōd* (Ps 68:22 'God will smite the crown/qodqōd of his enemies'; Hab 3:13; Deut 33:20; Num 24:17). The head-smiting (mḫṣ qdqd) is the central Chaoskampf victory-formula extending to Yahweh's defeat of his enemies and to Jael-vs-Sisera (Judg 5:26). Central entry `qdqd-head-smiting-victory-formula-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible`. The entry's rationale explicitly disavows the Christian-typology pre-resolution onto Gen 3:15 protoevangelium.

i18n.en: […] may she strike your crown [...]
You shall pour out your groaning, [O Prince Yammu],
you shall pour out your groaning, O Judge [Naharu …]
he took one [...]
[And] the Benevolent One, ʾIlu, [the kind-hearted, answered:]
[…] a servant am I, an attendant [...]
[ʾAṯiratu and her sons,] the goddess [and the household of her kindred],

notes.official: ʾAṯiratu, ʾIlu's consort and mother of the gods. **Direct Semitic cognate** of Hebrew Bible Asherah (1 Kgs 18:19 '450 prophets of Asherah'; Deut 16:21; the asherah-poles polemic). Central entry `athirat-asherah-mother-goddess-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible` (Day 2000; Olyan 1988; Hadley 2000; Dever 2005; Smith 2002). *bnh* 'her sons' = the divine assembly.

i18n.en: [how] can you strike Mighty Baʿlu [...]
[how] can you answer [Prince] Baʿlu [of the Earth?]

notes.official: *zbl bʿl ʾarṣ* 'Prince Baʿlu of the Earth' — *ʾarṣ* contested between 'earth' (default here) and 'underworld/netherworld' (Smith 1994 vol 1 reading, which prefigures the Môtu cycle in KTU 1.5-1.6). The Editor preserves 'of the Earth' as the literal default but the netherworld-reading would equally fit Baʿlu's later descent narratives.

i18n.en: […] the going of Baʿlu [...]
[…] go, O Yammu, your lord [...]
[furious was Prince] Baʿlu [...]
[…] Kothar [...]
[…] I shall call [...]

[KTU 1.2 col iv: top fragmentary; lower text is the most famous scene in the entire Cycle — the DUEL OF BAʿLU AND YAMMU. Kothar-wa-Khasis forges two magical mace-weapons named Yagrush ('Let-him-drive-out') and Ayamur ('Driver'); Baʿlu strikes Yammu twice; Yammu collapses; Baʿlu's kingship is proclaimed by ʿAṯtartu and the gods.]
[And] Kothar-wa-Khasis answered:

lines.translit: l rgmt . lk . l zbl . bʿl

i18n.en: Did I not declare to you, O Prince Baʿlu,
did I not repeat (it) to you, O Rider of the Clouds?

notes.official: **THE central epithet of Baʿlu.** *rkb ʿrpt* 'Rider of the Clouds' — MANDATORY cross-corpus with Hebrew Ps 68:5 *rōkēb bā-ʿărābôt*, Deut 33:26 *rōkēb šāmayim*, Ps 18:11 (YHWH-on-cherub-rides), Ps 104:3 (clouds-as-chariot), Isa 19:1. The Hebrew tradition's reassignment of Baʿlu's storm-theophany to Yahweh is **the textually clearest case** of Baʿlu-epithet-absorption into Yahwistic theology (Cross 1973; Day 2000). Central entry `rider-of-the-clouds-rkb-arpt-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible-storm-theophany` — entry's rationale explicitly disavows Christological pre-resolution onto Dan 7:13 / Mark 14:62 / Rev 1:7.

lines.translit: ht . ʾibk . bʿlm . ht . ʾibk . tmḫṣ

i18n.en: Now your enemy, O Baʿlu, now your enemy you shall strike;

lines.translit: ht . tṣmt . ṣrtk . tqḥ . mlk . ʿlmk

i18n.en: now you shall annihilate your foe. You shall take your eternal kingship,

notes.official: *mlk ʿlm* 'eternal kingship' — Kothar's promise to Baʿlu at the duel's threshold. MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew *malkût ʿōlām* (Ps 145:13); *melek ʿôlām* (Jer 10:10); Davidic *bayit u-mamlakhah ʿad-ʿolam* (2 Sam 7:13, 16); Dan 4:34, 7:14. The eternal-kingship formula is shared NW-Semitic royal-theology. Central entry `mlk-olam-eternal-king-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible`.

i18n.en: your dominion of generation upon generation.

notes.official: *dt drdrk* 'of generation upon generation' — structurally parallel to Hebrew *dōr wādôr / lədōr wādōr* (Ps 89:2, 4; Lam 5:19; Ps 145:13 *b-khol dor va-dor*). The doubled-generation-formula is one of the standard NW-Semitic eternal-rule expressions.

i18n.en: Kothar fashioned two maces,

notes.official: The weapon-forging scene begins. Kothar fashions (*yṣmd*) two maces (*ṣmdm*); the speech-act-naming follows in v.11. The scene is the **central speech-act-naming scene** in the chapter and the Ugaritic-side activation of the speech-act-efficacy tradition documented at the Adapa pass (Akkadian *aššum amat pī-šu* 'by the word of his mouth'). Central entry `yagrush-ayamur-speech-act-named-divine-weapons-cross-corpus`; speech-act-efficacy thesis at `speech-act-efficacy-language-power-of-life-and-death-cross-corpus`.

i18n.en: and he pro[claimed their (two) names]:

notes.official: *ypʿr šmthm* 'he proclaimed their names' — the speech-act-naming verb-formula. Same verb *pʿr* as ʾIlu's proclamation at 1.1-iv:15 (*w pʿr šm ym* 'he proclaimed Yammu's name'). The naming is performative — speaking the name **invests the weapon with its function**.

i18n.en: Your name, you, is Yagrush ('Let-him-drive-out')!

notes.official: **WEAPON NAME — Yagrush** (*ygrš*), the first mace, 'Let-him-drive-out' from G-yqtl of *grš* 'to drive out, expel'. The verb *grš* is the same root as Yahweh's expulsion of Adam from Eden (Gen 3:24 *va-y'garesh et ha-adam*) and Sarah's casting-out of Hagar (Gen 21:10), but the Editor does not pre-resolve to the Eden expulsion — the comparative-philology link is direct cognation, not theological-typology.

i18n.en: Yagrush — drive out Yammu!

notes.official: Kothar commands the weapon to perform exactly what its speech-act-name encodes — the weapon-name *is* the action. Speech becomes deed.

i18n.en: Drive out Yammu from his throne,
Naharu from the dais of his dominion!
You shall leap from the hand of Baʿlu,
like an eagle from his fingers!
Strike the shoulder of Prince Yammu,
between the hands (= chest) of Judge Naharu!
The mace leapt from the hand of Baʿlu,
like an eagle from his fingers.
It struck the shoulder of Prince Yammu,
between the hands of Judge Naharu.
But Yammu was strong; he did not collapse.

lines.translit: l tnġṣn . pnth . l ydlp . tmnh

i18n.en: His joints did not give way; his frame did not crumble.
Kothar arranged the two maces,
and proclaimed their (two) names:
Your name, you, is Ayamur ('Driver')!

notes.official: **WEAPON NAME — Ayamur** (*ʾaymr*), the second mace. Etymology debated: Smith 1994 vol 1 'May-he-drive-away' / 'Driver' (from *mwr* 'drive away'); Pardee 2003 'Expeller' (from *ʾamr* 'expel'); Gibson 1978 'All-Driver' (intensive). Default 'Driver'. The first mace strike (Yagrush at 1.2-iv:18) did not fell Yammu; Ayamur is the second and decisive blow at the crown (qdqd).

i18n.en: Ayamur — drive Yammu away!
Drive Yammu from his throne,
Naharu from the dais of his dominion!
You shall leap from the hand of Baʿlu,
like an eagle from his fingers!
Strike the crown of Prince Yammu,

notes.official: **THE killing blow.** *hlm qdqd* 'strike the crown' — the head-smiting victory-formula matched directly by Ps 68:22 *machatz rosh oyvav qodqōd* 'smash the head of his enemies, the crown'; Hab 3:13; Judg 5:26 (Jael strikes Sisera). Central entry `qdqd-head-smiting-victory-formula-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible`. The next line's *bn ʿnm* 'between the eyes' completes the killing-blow target-formula.

i18n.en: between the eyes of Judge Naharu!
Yammu collapsed; he fell to the earth.

notes.official: The Chaoskampf resolves with Yammu's collapse — Baʿlu's victory installs him in the eternal-kingship Kothar promised at v.8. The cross-corpus Chaoskampf cluster (central entry `chaoskampf-sea-conflict-cross-corpus-ugaritic-akkadian-hebrew-bible`) documents the Mesopotamian (Marduk-Tiamat), Ugaritic (Baʿlu-Yammu), and Hebrew (YHWH-Yam/Leviathan/Rahab) attestations.

i18n.en: His joints gave way; his frame crumbled.
Baʿlu drew (him in)(?), and he drained Yammu;

notes.official: The famous crux of the duel's resolution. *yqṯ* uncertain: 'gathers up / drags' (Smith 1994 vol 1), 'destroys' (some older), 'cuts off' (Pardee 2003 tentative). *yšt* from *šty* 'drink' yields 'and he drank Yammu' — a dismemberment/devouring image with possible wordplay on *ym* (sea / day / sea-drinkable); alternatively *yšt* could be reread as 'to set, place'. The Editor preserves Smith 1994 vol 1's '(drew in)(?), drained' rendering with explicit parenthetical-uncertainty. Compare Marduk-Tiamat scattering at Enuma Elish IV.

i18n.en: he made an end of Judge Naharu.
By name, ʿAṯtartu rebukes (him).

notes.official: The closing line. *tgʿrm* picks up the same *gʿr* 'rebuke' verb Baʿlu used against the cowering gods at 1.2-i:25 — the same lexeme as Hebrew *gāʿar* of YHWH's rebuke of the sea (Ps 18:15; 104:7; Isa 17:13; Nah 1:4). ʿAṯtartu's rebuke seals Baʿlu's victory and parallels the Hebrew YHWH-rebukes-sea pattern. Reading of *b šm* is contested: 'by name' (incantation; default here), 'with shame' (Pardee 2003 alternative), 'as for the name' (Smith 1994).
